votes.reasoning: AntigravityExecutor.swift now calls BoundedProcess.run. stdout and stderr are drained on separate threads (BoundedProcess.swift `drain`), stdout is capped at 4 MiB and triggers a kill when exceeded, stderr is capped at 64 KB and the rest is drained and dropped, and the timeout escalates SIGTERM, then 1 s, then SIGKILL. Reversal test: I restored HEAD's executor and added only the init params, with the timer using self.timeout. `large_stderr_completes_promptly` went RED (body empty, 3.09 s elapsed) and so did `oversized_stdout_rejected` (no 'exceeds 65536 bytes'). Both passed once the fix was restored. `classify` keeps the old error-mapping order. It also treats `terminationReason != .exit` as an error, which only makes explicit what a nonzero status already did.

Sources/AiTaskbarProviders/AntigravityExecutor.swift:75-104: the hand-written Process/Pipe/timer/continuation block (about 90 lines, 6 levels of nesting) is replaced by BoundedProcess.run plus a flat classify(_:) that throws instead of resuming a continuation in 7 places. Nesting drops from 6 to 3 levels. The stdout cap (maximumOutputBytes) and the stderr cap (static stderrBytes, with a comment giving the reason) are named and injectable. An oversized stdout becomes an AppError.io that users can see, not a silent truncation.

Sources/AiTaskbarProviders/AntigravityExecutor.swift:20-31: the new public init params (timeout 35, maximumOutputBytes 4 MiB) have defaults. The two existing call sites (GeminiProvider.swift:25,50) compile unchanged and the 35 s budget from HEAD is kept. The error classification in classify() is the same logic as before, moved out of the closure. The new AntigravityExecutorProcessTests.swift covers it.
